correctness.rationale: For one-dimensional graph F_m, a graph vertex is descending dominated precisely with exactly one earlier neighbor (even if its two neighbors are adjacent: a graph link has discrete vertices). If hub c has zero or at least two earlier neighbors, the induced matching has at most one of four directed leaf pairs D_i in each triangle, giving A=join_i D_i. If hub has exactly one earlier neighbor in triangle i, the directed hub pair h_i is present, no second pair in i, and the other triangles contribute only inward E_j, giving one of 2m cones h_i * (join_{j!=i} E_j). Each facet in A and each cone is realizable by an explicit vertex ordering, so this is exact equality of *full downward-closed* complexes, not containment. A is the join of m four-point discrete sets, hence wedge of 3^m spheres S^(m-1). Each B_i=join_{j!=i} E_j is S^(m-2), its inclusion into A is nullhomotopic since any vertex in D_i cones it in A; the 2m separate apex attachments add 2m spheres S^(m-1). m=1 gives six isolated points, hence reduced rank 5; m>=2 cofiber proof holds integrally. Disjoint face counting yields f_(k-1)=C(m,k)4^k+2m C(m-1,k-1)2^(k-1). Independently enumerated all vertex orders and full face sets at m=1,2,3; finite checks corroborate but do not replace the all-m join/cofiber argument.
